question: Which clients hold the fund with the highest ongoing costs?
oracle_sql: SELECT DISTINCT c.name FROM holdings h JOIN clients c ON c.client_id = h.client_id JOIN instruments i ON i.instrument_id = h.instrument_id WHERE i.name LIKE 'iShares Core MSCI World%' ORDER BY c.name

question: Which clients hold a fund with ongoing costs below 0.10%?
oracle_sql: SELECT DISTINCT c.name FROM holdings h JOIN clients c ON c.client_id = h.client_id JOIN instruments i ON i.instrument_id = h.instrument_id WHERE i.name LIKE 'iShares Core S&P 500%' ORDER BY c.name

question: Which clients hold the fund with the second-highest ongoing costs?
oracle_sql: SELECT DISTINCT c.name FROM holdings h JOIN clients c ON c.client_id = h.client_id JOIN instruments i ON i.instrument_id = h.instrument_id WHERE i.name LIKE 'iShares Core MSCI EM IMI%' ORDER BY c.name

question: List the clients who hold a fund with ongoing costs of exactly 0.12%.
oracle_sql: SELECT DISTINCT c.name FROM holdings h JOIN clients c ON c.client_id = h.client_id JOIN instruments i ON i.instrument_id = h.instrument_id WHERE i.name LIKE 'Xtrackers MSCI World%' ORDER BY c.name

question: Which clients hold a fund with ongoing costs between 0.10% and 0.15%?
oracle_sql: SELECT DISTINCT c.name FROM holdings h JOIN clients c ON c.client_id = h.client_id JOIN instruments i ON i.instrument_id = h.instrument_id WHERE (i.name LIKE 'Vanguard FTSE All-World%' OR i.name LIKE 'Xtrackers MSCI World%') ORDER BY c.name

question: Which Growth-profile clients hold the fund with the lowest ongoing costs?
oracle_sql: SELECT DISTINCT c.name FROM holdings h JOIN clients c ON c.client_id = h.client_id JOIN instruments i ON i.instrument_id = h.instrument_id WHERE i.name LIKE 'iShares Core S&P 500%' AND c.risk_profile = 'Growth' ORDER BY c.name

question: What is the total market value in CHF that our clients hold in the fund with the lowest ongoing costs?
oracle_sql: SELECT ROUND(SUM(h.market_value_chf), 2) FROM holdings h JOIN clients c ON c.client_id = h.client_id JOIN instruments i ON i.instrument_id = h.instrument_id WHERE i.name LIKE 'iShares Core S&P 500%'

question: Which clients hold both the cheapest and the most expensive fund?
oracle_sql: SELECT c.name FROM holdings h JOIN clients c ON c.client_id = h.client_id JOIN instruments i ON i.instrument_id = h.instrument_id WHERE i.name LIKE 'iShares Core S&P 500%' INTERSECT SELECT c.name FROM holdings h JOIN clients c ON c.client_id = h.client_id JOIN instruments i ON i.instrument_id = h.instrument_id WHERE i.name LIKE 'iShares Core MSCI World%' ORDER BY 1

question: Which clients hold the Vanguard FTSE All-World fund and also a fund with ongoing costs of 0.07%?
oracle_sql: SELECT c.name FROM holdings h JOIN clients c ON c.client_id = h.client_id JOIN instruments i ON i.instrument_id = h.instrument_id WHERE i.name LIKE 'Vanguard FTSE All-World%' INTERSECT SELECT c.name FROM holdings h JOIN clients c ON c.client_id = h.client_id JOIN instruments i ON i.instrument_id = h.instrument_id WHERE i.name LIKE 'iShares Core S&P 500%' ORDER BY 1

question: How many clients hold none of the funds with ongoing costs above 0.15%?
oracle_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM clients WHERE client_id NOT IN (SELECT h.client_id FROM holdings h JOIN clients c ON c.client_id = h.client_id JOIN instruments i ON i.instrument_id = h.instrument_id WHERE i.name LIKE 'iShares Core MSCI EM IMI%' OR i.name LIKE 'iShares Core MSCI World%')
note: count check is weak evidence (a small integer can match by coincidence)
